```{r}
#| label: setup-display
#| include: false

# Display-only render: read the completed D-SPIN CSV outputs without refitting,
# rewriting artifacts, or submitting jobs.
run_analysis <- FALSE

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(glue)
  library(knitr)
  library(DT)
})

wkdir <- "/resnick/groups/mthomson/jboktor/WILDRxSPF_brains"
dspin_dir <- file.path(wkdir, "data/interim/dspin")
manifest_f <- file.path(dspin_dir, "full_manifest.csv")
fit_summary_f <- file.path(dspin_dir, "fit_summary.csv")
weights_name <- file.path(
  "dspin_run",
  "gene_programs_total_20_onmf_20_prior_0_weights.csv"
)

read_if <- function(f) {
  if (file.exists(f)) {
    read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
  } else {
    NULL
  }
}

not_ready <- function(path) {
  cat(glue("Not yet computed — expected `{path}`. Run the upstream D-SPIN fit pipeline first.\n"))
}

manifest <- read_if(manifest_f)
fit_summary <- read_if(fit_summary_f)
has_index <- !is.null(manifest) && !is.null(fit_summary)

if (has_index) {
  unit_inventory <- manifest %>%
    select(
      unit_id, tissue, supertype_label, supertype_name,
      n_SPF, n_WildR, min_cells_per_sample_id, n_cells,
      n_genes, n_mast_genes, augur_auc, rank, run_tier
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      fit_summary %>% select(unit_id, status, method, elapsed_s),
      by = "unit_id"
    ) %>%
    arrange(tissue, supertype_name)

  ok_units <- unit_inventory %>%
    filter(status == "ok") %>%
    select(unit_id, tissue, supertype_label, supertype_name)
} else {
  unit_inventory <- tibble()
  ok_units <- tibble()
}

requested_unit <- params$unit_id
selected_unit <- if (
  nrow(ok_units) &&
  !is.null(requested_unit) &&
  requested_unit %in% ok_units$unit_id
) {
  requested_unit
} else if (nrow(ok_units)) {
  ok_units$unit_id[[1]]
} else {
  NA_character_
}

read_unit_csv <- function(relative_path) {
  if (!nrow(ok_units)) return(tibble())

  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(ok_units)), function(i) {
    f <- file.path(dspin_dir, ok_units$unit_id[[i]], relative_path)
    if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)

    read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(
        unit_id = ok_units$unit_id[[i]],
        tissue = ok_units$tissue[[i]],
        supertype_label = ok_units$supertype_label[[i]],
        supertype_name = ok_units$supertype_name[[i]],
        .before = 1
      )
  })
}

# Complete compact outputs across all successful units.
sample_meta_raw <- read_unit_csv("sample_meta.csv")
responses_raw <- read_unit_csv("responses.csv")
relative_responses_raw <- read_unit_csv("relative_responses.csv")
program_genes_raw <- read_unit_csv("programs_genes.csv")
network_raw <- read_unit_csv("network.csv")
program_annotations_raw <- read_unit_csv("program_annotations_david.csv")

unit_keys <- c("unit_id", "tissue", "supertype_label", "supertype_name")

animal_responses <- full_join(
  responses_raw,
  relative_responses_raw,
  by = c(unit_keys, "program_id", "sample_id")
) %>%
  left_join(
    sample_meta_raw %>%
      select(all_of(unit_keys), sample_id, microbiome, batch, if_control, n_cells),
    by = c(unit_keys, "sample_id")
  ) %>%
  arrange(tissue, supertype_name, program_id, microbiome, sample_id)

if (ncol(network_raw) >= 5) {
  names(network_raw)[5] <- "row_program"
}

# Complete oNMF gene/weight tables. These remain in the original wide layout:
# one row per within-program rank and paired <program>/Weights_<program> columns.
program_weights_raw <- read_unit_csv(weights_name)
if (nrow(program_weights_raw)) {
  program_weights_raw <- program_weights_raw %>%
    group_by(unit_id) %>%
    mutate(weight_rank = row_number(), .after = supertype_name) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Cell-level metadata are shown for one parameter-selected unit to keep the
# self-contained HTML from duplicating every nucleus across all unit tables.
selected_cells_f <- if (!is.na(selected_unit)) {
  file.path(dspin_dir, selected_unit, "cells_meta.csv")
} else {
  NA_character_
}
selected_cells <- if (!is.na(selected_cells_f) && file.exists(selected_cells_f)) {
  read_csv(selected_cells_f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(unit_id = selected_unit, .before = 1)
} else {
  tibble()
}

raw_dt <- function(x, caption, page_length = 10) {
  if (!nrow(x)) {
    cat("*Table is not available.*\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  datatable(
    x,
    rownames = FALSE,
    filter = "top",
    class = "compact stripe hover",
    extensions = "Buttons",
    caption = caption,
    options = list(
      pageLength = page_length,
      lengthMenu = c(10, 25, 50, 100, 500),
      scrollX = TRUE,
      deferRender = TRUE,
      dom = "Bfrtip",
      buttons = c("copy", "csv", "colvis")
    )
  )
}

fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
```

# Explore Raw D-SPIN Outputs for Single-Nucleus Data

## Overview

This notebook loads the complete saved tabular outputs from every successful single-nucleus D-SPIN fit and exposes them as searchable, sortable, downloadable tables. It keeps raw animal responses, SPF-centred responses, sample metadata, program genes and weights, program-interaction matrices, and DAVID program annotations available for exploratory visualization and figure construction without rerunning D-SPIN.

::: {.stat-row}
::: {.stat}
[`r fmt_n(nrow(ok_units))`]{.stat-value}
[Successful unit fits]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[`r fmt_n(nrow(animal_responses))`]{.stat-value}
[Animal × program rows]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[`r fmt_n(nrow(program_weights_raw))`]{.stat-value}
[Raw oNMF weight rows]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[`r fmt_n(nrow(network_raw))`]{.stat-value}
[Network matrix rows]{.stat-label}
:::
:::

## Background

The main D-SPIN analysis notebook reports calibrated animal-level tests and a focused set of figures. That is the right format for interpretation, but it intentionally hides most raw rows. Figure development often needs the opposite view: every animal-level response, every program's ranked genes and weights, and every coupling in each fitted network.

This explorer is read-only. It gathers the completed CSV outputs under [data/interim/dspin/]{.path}, preserves their raw values, and adds unit identifiers only where needed to combine the 140 per-unit files. The animal remains the unit of replication for WildR-versus-SPF comparisons.

## Results

::: {.callout-note}
## Choose a unit for cell-level metadata

All compact model outputs below include every successful unit and can be filtered by `unit_id`, tissue, cell type, program, animal, or gene. The large `cells_meta.csv` table is loaded for one unit at a time. The current unit is **`r selected_unit`**. To change it, render with:

`quarto render 0X_DSPIN-Output-Explorer_SN.qmd -P unit_id:<unit_id>`
:::

### Animal responses: raw h and SPF-centred relative h

```{r}
raw_dt(

)
```

### Full oNMF genes and weights

The original paired-column layout is retained. For program `0`, column `0` contains ranked genes and `Weights_0` contains their weights; the same pattern continues through program `19`. `weight_rank` is the original row order within a unit.

```{r}
#| label: cell-tbl-program-weights
#| echo: false

raw_dt(
  program_weights_raw,
  "Complete raw oNMF gene and weight tables for all 20 programs in every successful unit.",
  page_length = 25

```

[Source: cell `cell-tbl-program-weights`](#cell-tbl-program-weights){.provenance} · [data/interim/dspin/&lt;unit_id&gt;/dspin_run/gene_programs_total_20_onmf_20_prior_0_weights.csv]{.path}

### Program-interaction matrices

Each row is one row of the raw 20 × 20 **J** matrix. `row_program` identifies the source program; columns `P0`–`P19` contain its couplings to the target programs. Diagonal values are retained.

```{r}

#| echo: false

  "Complete raw D-SPIN network matrices across all successful units.",
```

## Next Steps

- **Done:** loaded the complete compact D-SPIN model outputs across all successful single-nucleus fits and made each table filterable and downloadable.
- Filter `animal_responses` to a unit or program before plotting; keep animal-level points visible rather than treating nuclei as independent replicates.
- Convert the selected unit's wide oNMF weights or **J** matrix to long form using the recipes below, then save finalized figures under [figures/DSPIN/snRNASeq/]{.path}.
- Use a new date-stamped filename for any derived table written to [tables/DSPIN/]{.path}; do not overwrite the fit outputs under [data/interim/dspin/]{.path}.

# Code & Provenance {.code-appendix}

The display tables above only read completed CSV artifacts. They do not fit models, write tables, or submit jobs. The setup cell combines per-unit outputs by adding `unit_id`, tissue, and Allen supertype columns; response values, weights, and couplings are unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: cell-fig-response-recipe
#| eval: false

# Figure recipe: animal × program heatmap for the selected unit.
response_plot_data <- animal_responses %>%
  filter(unit_id == selected_unit) %>%
  mutate(
    microbiome = factor(microbiome, c("SPF", "WildR")),
    sample_id = fct_reorder(sample_id, as.integer(microbiome))
  )

ggplot(response_plot_data, aes(sample_id, program_id, fill = relative_h)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_grid(. ~ microbiome, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scico::scale_fill_scico(palette = "vik", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(
    title = selected_unit,
    x = "Animal",
    y = "D-SPIN program",
    fill = "Relative h"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-fig-network-recipe
#| eval: false

# Figure recipe: long-form J matrix for the selected unit.
network_plot_data <- network_raw %>%
  filter(unit_id == selected_unit) %>%
  select(row_program, starts_with("P")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    starts_with("P"),
    names_to = "column_program",
    values_to = "J"
  )

ggplot(network_plot_data, aes(column_program, row_program, fill = J)) +
  geom_tile() +
  coord_equal() +
  scico::scale_fill_scico(palette = "vik", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(
    title = selected_unit,
    x = "Target program",
    y = "Source program",
    fill = "J"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-fig-weights-recipe
#| eval: false

# Figure recipe: unpack the original wide weight table and plot one program.
unit_weights <- program_weights_raw %>%
  filter(unit_id == selected_unit)

weights_long <- map_dfr(0:19, function(k) {
  tibble(
    program_id = paste0("P", k),
    gene = unit_weights[[as.character(k)]],
    weight = as.numeric(unit_weights[[paste0("Weights_", k)]])
  )
}) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gene), nzchar(gene), !is.na(weight))

weights_long %>%
  filter(program_id == "P0") %>%
  slice_max(weight, n = 20) %>%
  mutate(gene = fct_reorder(gene, weight)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(weight, gene)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = glue("{selected_unit}: P0"),
    x = "oNMF weight",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
